desc:
Flutter app development for iOS and Android lets you launch on both stores from one codebase. Ecom Swift LLC builds your app in Flutter and Dart, tests it on real phones, prepares both store releases in your own accounts and hands over the full source code.

## What is Flutter app development?

Flutter is a toolkit from Google for building apps with the Dart language. You write the interface and logic once, and the same project compiles into an iPhone app and an Android app. Flutter draws its own interface rather than wrapping each system's controls, which is why the two apps can look and behave the same.

For a buyer, the practical meaning is simple. One project, one set of screens to design, one set of features to test, and two store listings at the end. You are not paying for the same app twice.

## Why build for both platforms with one codebase

Your audience rarely lives on a single system. If you build only for iPhone, you lose every Android user, and the reverse. Two separate native builds solve that, but they double the design work, the testing and every future change.

With one Flutter codebase, a new button or a fixed bug reaches both groups in the same release. Features stay in step, so support does not have to explain why the Android version lacks something the iPhone version has. For a small business or a startup, that consistency is often more valuable than the last bit of platform-specific polish.

## How a well-built app affects your results

An app earns its place when people open it again. That depends on speed, clarity and trust. A screen that responds instantly, a sign-in that works first time and a layout that fits the phone in someone's hand all keep users inside the app long enough to see its value.

Build quality also affects your costs after launch. Clean structure, sensible state handling and tested flows make later features cheaper to add. A rushed app with tangled code turns every update into a risk. The work done in the first build decides how much you pay for the second.

## What a great Flutter app includes

- A written list of screens and features, agreed before any code is written.
- A consistent theme: colors, type, spacing and reusable widgets.
- Navigation that suits both platforms, including the back gesture people expect.
- Local data storage for settings and content that must survive a restart.
- Sign-in with email, Google or Apple where the app needs accounts.
- A connection to your backend or API, with clear handling of errors and slow networks.
- Push notifications set up for both iOS and Android where needed.
- An app icon and splash screen that match your brand.
- Test builds delivered through TestFlight and Google Play internal testing.
- Clean, commented source code in a repository you own.

## How we build your app

We start with a short written plan: the screens, the features and anything left out on purpose. Once you approve it, we build in small steps and send test builds so you can tap through real screens early, not at the end.

We test on physical iPhones and Android phones across different OS versions, because simulators miss things. Then we prepare the release builds, store listing text and the required privacy answers, and enter them in your Apple Developer and Google Play accounts. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in number of screens, sign-in and backend work, purchases and the level of release support. Whether a store accepts the app is decided by Apple and Google, so we build to their published rules and fix what a reviewer asks for.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide the one job your app must do well before you list features.
- Collect your logo, colors and any reference apps you like.
- Test the builds we send on your own phone and report what you see.
- Open the developer accounts early, as approval can take time.
- Keep a short list of things for a later version.

**Avoid:**
- Adding features mid-build without agreeing their effect on scope.
- Copying another app's design so closely that a reviewer or lawyer could object.
- Collecting user data you do not need.
- Skipping real-device testing on older phones.
- Leaving store accounts and tax details until launch day.

## Who this service is for

A small business owner who wants a customer app for bookings or orders on both phone systems. A founder with a clear idea who wants a polished first release rather than a prototype. An agency or a company without mobile developers that needs a reliable build partner and wants to own the result.

## What we need from you

A short description of what the app should do, any designs or examples you like, your brand assets and details of the service or API it should connect to. For the stores, you will need an Apple Developer account and a Google Play Console account in your name. We never ask for passwords. We work as a team member, developer user or collaborator in the accounts and repositories where the platform allows it, and we confirm the plan in writing before we start.
